clue.text: Sweet, thrifty gal ignored what the midwife might say (9, 17, 18, 19A, 25, 27 and 32?)

indicators.note: ignored tells us the word gal is dropped from the thrifty word, leaving its first three letters

parts.note: thrifty means frugal
taken as written
a midwife announcing a boy's birth says 'it's a lad'

explanation.surface: A careful young woman skips something while a midwife announces a birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' takes GAL off FRUGAL, leaving FRU. The bracketed numbers point to the answers that are anagrams of fruits (DAMSON, PEARS, MANGO, PEACH, DATES, GRAPE, TANGERINES): a mixed bowl of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert of chopped mixed fruit is a classic British pudding, so it counts as a sweet course.

clue.text: Bill includes a chap (Charlie) one's engaged

indicators.note: includes means the bill word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a bill is a fee charged
Ian is a man's name, a chap
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An invoice mentions a man called Charlie who is about to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who is betrothed is one who is engaged to be married.

clue.text: Youngsters heading off for better times

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the youngsters word is removed

parts.note: pups are young animals, youngsters

explanation.surface: Young people leave for a happier period.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'ups and downs' makes the plural mean good spells or better times.

clue.text: Sprinter's three from the end before competition raised level

indicators.note: three from the end asks for the final three letters of the sprinter word

parts.note: a race is a competition

explanation.surface: A runner's position before a contest on a raised platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a flat raised bank or step of ground, a level above the surroundings.

clue.text: Girl with nothing on's rubbish — or does she add gloss?

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
nothing is zero, the letter O
tat is cheap rubbish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A naked girl is mocked as rubbish, or is she glamorous?
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'on' simply join the pieces in order; the gloss is a scholarly note, not lip gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloss is an explanatory note in a text, and someone writing such notes adds glosses.

clue.text: Paddy shows this nativity scene after missing mass

indicators.note: after missing says the mass letter is dropped from the nativity word

parts.note: the manger is the centrepiece of a nativity scene
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: An Irishman displays a crib scene after skipping church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irishman (and pairs with 'mass'), but it is the British word for a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a paddy is a tantrum or fit of rage.

clue.text: Dirk's nuts passed round

indicators.note: passed round signals the crazy word is turned to read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy, nuts

explanation.surface: A man called Dirk's nuts are handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirk' reads as a man's name; it is a dagger, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To dirk someone is to strike them with a dagger, which is to knife them.

clue.text: He winds up meeting in the middle to make progress

indicators.note: in the middle picks the central letter of the seven-letter meeting word

parts.note: to roll is to move steadily along, make progress

explanation.surface: A man ends a gathering halfway through so things can move on.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet provocateur posts things meant to irritate, deliberately annoying others.

clue.text: Out of love, follow former pop star

indicators.note: out of says the love letter goes out of the follow word

parts.note: to obey is to follow orders
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
once means formerly, former

explanation.surface: No longer in love, someone trails an ex-singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'former' seems to describe the pop star, but it gives ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The American singer known by her first name is one of the biggest names in pop music.

clue.text: We travel with bananas in small numbers

indicators.note: in places the crazy word inside the numbers abbreviation

parts.note: nos is the short form of numbers
bananas is slang for mad

explanation.surface: A few of us go about carrying bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also an anagram of DAMSON, one of the fruits of 1 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanderers with no fixed home are people who keep moving, so they would say 'we travel'.

clue.text: A chap going round endlessly grumpy — there's no place for it

indicators.note: going round means the chap's name encloses the grumpy word

parts.note: Alan is a chap's name

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter of the grumpy word

parts.note: sore can mean irritable, grumpy

explanation.surface: An irritable man pacing about has nowhere to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' is the racing sense: finishing in the first few.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or runner that fails to finish in a placed position is a loser in the race.

clue.text: With origin unseen, age old record's unknown? Not in this field

indicators.note: with origin unseen drops the first letter of the word age

parts.note: taken as written
a log is a written record
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Ancient records are a mystery, but not in this discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue is a wink: in this science the age-old record of the rocks is exactly what is known.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth science is a field of study, and the clue's 'this field' names that discipline.

clue.text: Domain's master giving us a small sign

parts.note: com is the familiar internet domain suffix
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A web domain owner gives us a modest signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark marking a short pause is a small written sign.

clue.text: I sat where the minotaur was and I have large ears

indicators.note: sat means the letter I is seated inside the labyrinth word

parts.note: the Minotaur lived in the labyrinth, a maze

explanation.surface: Someone sat in the Minotaur's home, and has big ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn grows in large cobs called ears, so the crop speaks of its large ears.

clue.text: Pitch originally has man batting to cover

parts.note: pitch was originally the dark sticky residue we call tar
Paul is a man's name
in cricket the side batting is in

explanation.surface: At first the cricket pitch has a man batting to protect it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like the cricket field in a scene of covering it; it is the black substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy waterproof sheet is used to cover things such as a cricket square.

clue.text: I dozed, second dropping off in very long film — it might be fitting for me

definitions.text: it might be fitting for me

indicators.note: in places the dozing pieces inside the long film word

parts.note: an epic is a very long film

indicators.note: dropping off says the second letter-abbreviation leaves the dozed word

parts.note: dozed means slept

explanation.surface: Someone nodded off during a very long film, which they felt suited them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitting' is the pun: having fits, not suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a seizure disorder may suffer fits, so for them fitting is a symptom.

clue.text: Mr German has yen to be in epic at sea — an alternative to 1A?

indicators.note: to be in puts the German title and yen inside the shuffled letters
at sea means confused, so the letters of epic are rearranged

parts.note: Herr is the German for Mr
Y is the symbol for the yen

explanation.surface: A German gentleman longs to star in an epic set on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' shuffles epic, and 'to be in' sets the German title and the yen symbol inside that shuffle, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked dessert filled with fruit could be chosen instead of a bowl of mixed fruit for pudding.

clue.text: Remaining bit of sangria to diminish gradually

indicators.note: bit of takes just the opening letter of sangria

parts.note: to pare is to trim away little by little

explanation.surface: Drinking the sangria a little at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also an anagram of PEARS, a fruit for 1 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left over or surplus is extra, still remaining after use.

clue.text: A garden ornament with bit chipped off is put back in the middle

indicators.note: put back signals the chipped ornament is reversed, in a down entry read upwards
with bit chipped off removes the final letter of the ornament

parts.note: a gnome is a classic garden ornament

explanation.surface: A chipped garden gnome is returned to the middle of the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: GNOME loses its E to give GNOM, which turns to MONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Being surrounded by others means being amid them, in the middle of the group.

clue.text: Discounted old icon aide's returned

parts.note: Che Guevara, the revolutionary, is an old icon on posters

indicators.note: returned signals the assistant word is read backwards

parts.note: a PA, personal assistant, is an aide

explanation.surface: A cut-price old religious image an assistant took back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'icon' suggests a religious painting; it is Che Guevara. The answer is also an anagram of PEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are discounted are reduced in price, so inexpensive.

clue.text: A really good joke perhaps? Unlikely in this!

definitions.text: A really good joke perhaps? Unlikely in this!

parts.words: A really good joke perhaps? Unlikely in this!
parts.note: a first-rate thing is called by this slang word, yet the paper-wrapped party favour pulled at Christmas holds notoriously bad jokes

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a fine joke will ever turn up somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: British Christmas crackers are pulled at the table and contain a groan-worthy joke on a slip of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls an excellent thing a corker, and the festive novelty contains a weak joke.

clue.text: Fruit's not left by stuff that's cold as stone

indicators.note: not says the left letter is not present in the fruit word

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
ice is frozen, cold stuff

explanation.surface: A fruit sits beside something stone-cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A light porous volcanic rock is a type of stone used for scrubbing.

clue.text: Once again makes use of mere rehashed stratagems

indicators.note: rehashed means reworked, so the letters of mere are rearranged

parts.note: ploys are tactics or stratagems

explanation.surface: A firm reuses the same tired schemes.
explanation.definitionFit: To hire someone back is to engage their services anew, using them again.

clue.text: Basic camping equipment is put up — shut up about it

indicators.note: about says the penned-in word goes round the jumbled letters

parts.note: pent means shut up or confined

indicators.note: up as in stirred up signals the letters of put are mixed

explanation.surface: Simple camping kit gets erected while someone is told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reads like erecting the tent, but 'up' is an anagram signal working on put, and 'about' wraps the shut-up word round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A small two-person ridge shelter is the most basic kind of camping gear.

clue.text: Tired running about on board ship with steps like these?

indicators.note: on board places the jumbled letters within the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: running about suggests disorder, so the letters of tired are rearranged

explanation.surface: Weary passengers rush around a ship's deck taking big paces.
explanation.definitionFit: Long purposeful steps are the kind meant by this plural, as in walking with great paces.

clue.text: I gather together burning coal left inside by idiot

parts.note: an ass is an idiot

indicators.note: inside puts the left letter within the burning coal word

parts.note: an ember is a burning coal

explanation.surface: A fool leaves a hot coal in the grate while gathering things.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts parts or people together is the one who gathers them together.

clue.text: Sorry about the empty place

indicators.note: about means the sorry word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: sorry can mean sad or pitiful

indicators.note: empty clears out the middle of the word the, keeping its outer letters

explanation.surface: Regret about an empty spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also an anagram of DATES, a fruit for 1 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: Used in 'in his stead', the word means place or role taken by another.

clue.text: Undesirable to drive back to the North

indicators.note: to the North signals reading upwards in this down entry, a reversal

parts.note: to repel is to drive back

explanation.surface: An unwelcome person must be pushed back north.
explanation.definitionFit: A social outcast shunned by others is figuratively a pariah, an undesirable.

clue.text: It relays message about vacant space for reversing

indicators.note: for reversing signals both words that precede it are read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a gap is an empty space

explanation.surface: A notice about a free parking space for backing into.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also an anagram of GRAPE, a fruit for 1 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleeper is a small device that receives and passes on short messages.

clue.text: I'll leave distraught peacenik, one guarding a joint

indicators.note: distraught means in turmoil, so the letters of peacenik are rearranged after one goes

parts.note: I'll says I will leave, giving the single letter to remove

explanation.surface: Someone vows to walk out on a distressed pacifist who guards a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: PEACENIK without I is rearranged; 'leave' says the I goes. 'joint' tempts as a pub or cannabis; it is the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is a bone that sits in front of the knee and protects that joint.

clue.text: Happy place's become a bed of roses

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place in addresses
a bed of roses is an easy situation, so things have eased

explanation.surface: A cheerful home has turned into a life of comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling glad or satisfied is a near synonym of happy.

clue.text: A tabloid mired in misunderstandings

indicators.note: mired in means stuck inside, so the answer sits within the long word

explanation.surface: A gossip paper gets bogged down in confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known British red-top newspaper is a popular tabloid.

clue.text: Ill-bred prig with no power

indicators.note: with no says the power letter is taken away from the prig word

parts.note: a prude is a prig
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A boorish prig has lost all authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad-mannered and impolite behaviour is what ill-bred describes.

clue.text: South Americans: a right gallant chap and Spanish lady

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a gallant chap
Ines is a Spanish woman's name

explanation.surface: A courteous man and a Spanish woman, both from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also an anagram of TANGERINES, the last fruit for 1 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the nation south of Brazil, with Buenos Aires its capital, are South Americans.
